definitions.gloss: to pile up; to accumulate; to build up
definitions.explanation: For things to stack up or accumulate over time, either physically (objects) or abstractly (experience, stress, effort).

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れが{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なっている。
{小|ちい}さな{努力|どりょく}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なって、{大|おお}きな{成果|せいか}になる。
examples.english: Small efforts accumulate and become great results.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{不満|ふまん}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なり、ついに{爆発|ばくはつ}した。
examples.english: Years of frustration had piled up and finally exploded.

notes:
A compound verb combining {積|つ}む (to pile up) and {重|かさ}なる (to overlap, to stack). The intransitive form — things accumulate on their own or over time. Commonly used both for physical stacking and metaphorical accumulation of experiences, effort, stress, or grievances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経験|けいけん}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なる — experience accumulates
- {努力|どりょく}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なる — efforts build up
- {疲労|ひろう}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なる — fatigue piles up
- {不満|ふまん}が{積|つ}み{重|かさ}なる — frustration builds up

TRANSITIVE PAIR:
- {積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる — to pile up, to accumulate (transitive); used when someone deliberately builds up something

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たまる — to accumulate, to build up; more casual and general
- {蓄積|ちくせき}する — to accumulate; more formal/technical
- {重|かさ}なる — to overlap, to pile up; one of the component verbs, less emphasis on gradual accumulation
